Package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend

@NullMarked package io.github.jabrena.juno.backend
Code generation: turns optimized Juno IR into a complete Arduino sketch, generated assembly plus the C++ runtime shim it links against, for every supported board.

This package holds what both code generators share: frame and program layout, the calling convention and IntrinsicLowering. io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.thumb2 generates GNU ARM Thumb-2 assembly for the UNO R4 WiFi and the UNO Q, io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.avr AVR assembly for the UNO WiFi Rev2. Both assemble the shim through io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.runtime, and reach a board's ArduinoCore only through CoreRuntime.

Dependencies point one way: the code generators depend on the runtime, the per-core implementations depend on the shared runtime, and both depend on the contracts in runtime.spi, which depend on nothing else in the backend.

    AsmBackend

    Every value/local's fixed stack offset, and the total (8-byte-aligned) frame size to reserve.
    GeneratedCode
    What a backend generates for one program.
    IntrinsicLowering
    Lowers each IrInstruction.IntrinsicCall to assembly.
    IntrinsicTarget
    The instruction-set half of IntrinsicLowering: the intrinsic table says which runtime function an intrinsic calls with which argument words, and an implementation says how one such call, and the few intrinsics that touch memory directly, look in its assembly.
    ProgramLayout
    Whole-program storage decisions made before any code is emitted: arena object sizes and field offsets, mutable static fields' .bss symbols, and the .rodata symbols of string literals and compiler-generated constant int arrays — plus the data sections holding them.
    ProgramLayout.DataDirectives
    The assembler directives a data section is written with: word emits 32-bit values (ARM's .word; AVR's .word is 16-bit, so it uses .long), align 4-byte-aligns, and bss switches to the zero-initialized section (AVR's assembler has no .bss shorthand).
    StackFrameSizing
    Authoritative target-backend stack sizing shared with static runtime-risk analysis.
    WordSource
    One argument word of a call: Juno's calling convention passes every argument as 32-bit words, in order.
